items.label: f01-review-log-ignore-duplicates
items.front: Review logs are pushed with upsert(..., { ignoreDuplicates: true }) while decks, notes and cards go through per-row RPCs (engine.ts:119-129). Why is ignoreDuplicates the right choice for logs?
items.back: Review logs are append-only history: a retried push after a lost response must not duplicate or overwrite an existing log, so a duplicate insert is simply ignored - idempotent by id.

items.label: f03-schema-change-steps
items.front: What are the steps to change the schema safely in this local-first app, and what is the senior question behind them?
items.back: Update TS types; add a NEW Dexie version migration (never edit version 1 destructively); add a Supabase migration; update merge/import/export; test old data, new data and sync conflicts. Senior question: what data exists offline that the server has never seen yet?

items.label: f02-markdown-url-policy
items.front: MarkdownView skips raw HTML. Why does the risk register still list Markdown as an XSS/phishing risk?
items.back: skipHtml only drops raw HTML; the link and image URL policy is left implicit (whatever the Markdown library does by default), and nothing in the repo pins it. Make the protocol allowlist explicit (e.g. http/https/mailto) and add a malicious-URL test - the register rates this Medium confidence, a hypothesis to verify.

items.prompt: A user signs in on a device whose local rows already carry a DIFFERENT user_id. What does adoptLocalData do?

choices.text: It refuses to adopt and records auth_blocked
It deletes the foreign rows and keeps the local-only ones
It reassigns every local row to the newly signed-in user
It adopts rows with a null user_id and ignores the rest

choices: It refuses to adopt and records auth_blocked
It deletes the foreign rows and keeps the local-only ones
It reassigns every local row to the newly signed-in user
It adopts rows with a null user_id and ignores the rest

items.explanation: Any row whose user_id is set and differs from uid blocks adoption, so one account cannot inherit another's local data; only otherwise are null-owned rows assigned. The guides flag that this path has no tests yet.

items.prompt: Sync keeps failing because the server is down. How does the retry delay evolve?

choices.text: It stops retrying after three failures until the next sign-in
It retries immediately in a loop until the network returns
A fixed retry every 60 s, driven only by the interval timer
It doubles from 5 s up to a 5-minute cap, resetting on success

choices: It stops retrying after three failures until the next sign-in
It retries immediately in a loop until the network returns
A fixed retry every 60 s, driven only by the interval timer
It doubles from 5 s up to a 5-minute cap, resetting on success

items.explanation: On error the last_error is stored, a retry timer is scheduled with backoffMs, and backoffMs = Math.min(backoffMs * 2, 300_000); success sets it back to 5_000.

choices.text: The note is marked converted but its cards are missing
Nothing is saved, because Dexie rolls back the dialog session
The cards are created a second time when the dialog reopens
Cards exist but the note is not marked converted

choices: The note is marked converted but its cards are missing
Nothing is saved, because Dexie rolls back the dialog session
The cards are created a second time when the dialog reopens
Cards exist but the note is not marked converted

items.explanation: createCard and markConverted run from the UI as separate writes; the fix moves create + mark into one repository transaction helper with a partial-failure test.

items.prompt: A card is edited five times while offline. How many outbox entries exist for it?

choices.text: Zero, because offline edits go straight into the pull cursor
Two: one for the first edit and one for the latest
Five, replayed in order when the device reconnects
One, with its queued_at refreshed on each edit

choices: Zero, because offline edits go straight into the pull cursor
Two: one for the first edit and one for the latest
Five, replayed in order when the device reconnects
One, with its queued_at refreshed on each edit

items.explanation: enqueueOutbox finds the existing [table_name+row_id] entry and only updates queued_at; push reads the CURRENT row, so one entry syncs the latest state - an idempotency property.

items.prompt: Grading a card writes the card, a review log and outbox entries. Why does applyReview put all of them in one Dexie transaction?

choices.text: So a crash cannot leave a review half-written or unqueued for sync
Because the outbox entry must exist before the card row is written
Because Dexie allows only one table write per transaction otherwise
To batch the IndexedDB requests so the write completes faster

choices: So a crash cannot leave a review half-written or unqueued for sync
Because the outbox entry must exist before the card row is written
Because Dexie allows only one table write per transaction otherwise
To batch the IndexedDB requests so the write completes faster

items.explanation: Card + review log + two outbox entries commit together; the outbox is how offline changes are guaranteed to reach the server later.

choices.text: Only the newer of the two edits; the other is lost
Both versions, stored as two separate cards
A's text with the SRS state from before either change
A's new text and B's new scheduling state

choices: Only the newer of the two edits; the other is lost
Both versions, stored as two separate cards

A's new text and B's new scheduling state

items.explanation: mergeCard compares content_updated_at and srs_updated_at independently (ties go to remote), so text edits and reviews merge without clobbering each other.

choices.text: Cards are encrypted per user, so foreign rows are unreadable anyway
The anon key is scoped to one user, so other rows are invisible
It is: Supabase rejects any query that omits a user_id filter
Client filters can be omitted; Postgres RLS is the real guard

choices: Cards are encrypted per user, so foreign rows are unreadable anyway
The anon key is scoped to one user, so other rows are invisible
It is: Supabase rejects any query that omits a user_id filter
Client filters can be omitted; Postgres RLS is the real guard

items.explanation: IDOR prevention lives server-side in RLS policies on every synced table; the client filter is a convenience, not authorization.

items.prompt: A learner grades a card and immediately presses Undo. What does undoReview do to sync state?

choices.text: Rolls back the original Dexie transaction from its saved handle
Restores the card, deletes the log, and drops the log's outbox entry
Appends a compensating negative review log and pushes both of them
Only restores the card; the review log still syncs to the server later

choices: Rolls back the original Dexie transaction from its saved handle
Restores the card, deletes the log, and drops the log's outbox entry
Appends a compensating negative review log and pushes both of them
Only restores the card; the review log still syncs to the server later

items.explanation: Undo is compensation, not rollback: one new transaction puts cardBefore with a fresh srs_updated_at, deletes the log and its outbox row.

choices.text: Client clocks and late offline pushes would let rows fall behind the cursor
Client updated_at is not stored in the Supabase tables at all
server_updated_at is indexed while updated_at is not, so it is only faster
Using updated_at would download each user's own rows twice per sync

choices: Client clocks and late offline pushes would let rows fall behind the cursor
Client updated_at is not stored in the Supabase tables at all
server_updated_at is indexed while updated_at is not, so it is only faster

items.explanation: A device that was offline for a day pushes rows with old client times; a cursor on client time would skip them forever.

choices.text: The in-flight sync is cancelled and restarted from scratch
It gets the in-flight promise; no second loop starts
The second call throws a 'sync already running' error

items.explanation: if (running) return running; - the module-level promise makes sync single-flight and clears itself in finally.

items.prompt: During a pull, a remote card arrives whose deck is not in the local database yet. What happens to it?

choices.text: The whole pull fails and is retried with backoff
A placeholder deck is created so the card can be saved
It is skipped, while the cursor still advances past it
It is saved with a null deck_id and fixed on the next sync

choices: The whole pull fails and is retried with backoff
A placeholder deck is created so the card can be saved
It is skipped, while the cursor still advances past it
It is saved with a null deck_id and fixed on the next sync

items.explanation: if (!deck) break; inside mergeRows, while the per-table cursor moves to the last row of the page - so the card can stay missing until it changes again. The register suggests buffering/retrying or pulling decks first.
